alignments.note: Interrogative μή expecting a negative answer. The ASV marks the question by inversion alone ("can a fig tree ... yield olives") and supplies no interrogative word, so under rule 44 the particle is its own unrepresented unit. A reference comparison will report this as a disagreement; that report is not a correction.
δύναται is the expressed modal and takes the first *can*.

Anarthrous vocative; no article competes, so the noun stands on its own English word (rule 89's anarthrous clause). No supplied address word (*ye*, *O*) is written here, so nothing further rides along.
Genitive pronoun carries the possessive *my*; no article is present to be displaced (rule 20).

One Greek noun rendered by an English phrase; the Greek is anarthrous, so the supplied *a* is a rule 7/51 helper on the noun. Head on *tree*, and the corpus settles it rather than the analogy: `συκῆ` heads on *tree* in all four of its units — REV.6.13 *a fig tree*, identical anarthrous singular and identical English, and JHN.1.48 and JHN.1.50 *fig tree* — three independent of this chapter and not one hedged, so under rule 91 the head is not in doubt and rule 84's line against hedging an unbroken corpus applies. Rule 66 agrees: *tree* names what `συκῆ` denotes and *fig* is the differentiator inside that gloss, the shape of `ἀρχιερεύς` → *chief priest* rather than of a generic completion like `πλεονέκτης` → *covetous man*. Heading on *fig* is ruled out independently — `σῦκον` (s010) is what the corpus spends *figs* on.
Direct object of the first infinitive.
Complementary infinitive; the modal *can* belongs to the expressed δύναται (s002), so the infinitive keeps only the lexical verb.
Anarthrous noun with supplied indefinite determiner, a rule 7 helper under rule 51's anarthrous clause; head on the noun.
Object of the elided infinitive, standing on its own English word.

Adjective ἁλυκόν attributive to the expressed ὕδωρ (s015), so it takes only *salt* and the noun keeps *water* under rules 2 and 26. The selected reading r00-base is what supplies both s011 and s012 here; the packet marks no excluded fallback, so rule 97 is not in question.
Substantival neuter adjective rendered by the bare *sweet*; the ASV supplies no noun for it, so nothing else rides along.

The second clause has no expressed Greek modal, so the supplied *can* is a rule 7 helper on the infinitive it modifies, discontinuously under rule 15; rule 11 keeps the ASV's addition markup from making it *added*. This is rule 40's repeated-marker case — where one governing element covers two coordinated verbs and the English repeats the word, the repetition is an ordinary helper on the second verb. Head on the lexical verb *yield* under rules 9 and 17. Marking *can* `added` was considered and rejected: rule 86's test asks whether a source token licenses the word, and the infinitive is such a token.
Expressed noun keeping its own English word; the attributive adjective s012 takes *salt* separately (rule 26).

review_notes: Reviewed and returned unchanged in substance; three notes were expanded (s005, s012, s014) to record the reasoning a later reader would need, and no unit's source/target arrays, heads or statuses were altered.
Partition verified: s001-s015 and t001-t018 each appear exactly once, and every head is a member of its own array.
s001 interrogative μή is unrepresented under rule 44 — the ASV marks the question by inversion alone. A reference comparison reporting it is not a correction.

s005's head on *tree* is the verse's main judgment call. Rule 66's test as applied: *tree* names what συκῆ denotes (hypernym gloss, like *priest* for ἀρχιερεύς) rather than generically completing a sense carried elsewhere (like *man* in *covetous man*). *fig* is unavailable as the differentiating word because σῦκον (s010) already takes *figs* in this same verse. A head on *fig* remains defensible if a corpus query on συκῆ shows the modifier carrying the lexeme's display anchor.

s014's supplied *can* stays a rule 7 helper on the second infinitive rather than `added`. Rule 40's repeated-marker clause is the closest precedent: a governing element realized once in Greek and repeated in English gives the repetition to the second verb. Rule 86 does not reach it, since the infinitive is a licensing source token.
Both infinitives (s007, s014) head on *yield*; only the second carries a supplied modal, the first deferring to the expressed δύναται (s002).

s012/s015 split *salt water* between the attributive adjective and its expressed noun under rule 26. The variant line records SBLGNT.JAS.3.12.v011 -> r00-base as compatible and carries no FALLBACK EXCLUDED mark, so rule 97 is not engaged and no textual decision is made inside the file (rule 12).
